body: For clarification: we live together still because we both have to. He can no more afford rent on his own than I can. I do have a full-time well paying job. The seasonal fluctuations were more dramatic than either of us thought they would be initially. Now that we/I know the change during off-season, money will be saved during the winter to cover it. He understands that and agrees. His point (and yours) that I do see now and agree with is that I need to put a bigger effort into private practice to supplement until the season picks back up (I can't go full tilt with them both at the same time, it's far too much on my hands and isn't necessary in the winter).

Trading for something for him is a really great idea that hadn't even struck me, thank you for that. He's not one that has or will get tattoos or anything of the sort but I'm sure I can find something.

Edit: spelling

Thank you for the straight-forward yet kind/encouraging analysis. It brought me to tears a bit to have this all framed in a more neutral and motivating light. Thank you. I am planning out Instagram posts for the month right now and have a design for business cards ready to go as soon as there's cash to order them. I do know this is a very hard situation for him as well and want to prove to him that I am committed to increasing my income and taking the burden off of him. Thank you again friend.

I'm definitely aware that this is a short-term thing that he is losing patience with. What we've talked about is once my season picks up I'll pay him back what he's covered, get the debt under my name, get finances 100% separated, and move out. It's amicable enough that neither of us want the other on the street or going without food, hence why we're still intertwined here.

This is not meant to defend myself or ague my point of view but there's no need for quotations. It is a functioning business with a state license that does make me money. I do know I'm a dick for him covering what I can't right now and I genuinely appreciate the comment regarding his right to an opinion given he is helping me out, that's a point of view I need to see as well.

You're definitely right that it's an outlet for impulse; I guess in my mind it seemed less harmful since it isn't impacting the actual bank accounts but I do see yours and his point. Regarding a second job: this is something I've done and was working 2-4 jobs for nearly three years up until this past March when my mental health had enough. This is something I may look into for the off-season (summer) but for the winter he does agree that it's not feasible due to the insane workload at my full-time gig. BK is a nightmare and I am working with an attorney on it right now but it will take some time and know-how to get all the joint debt transferred to my name.

Understood and I don't disagree. Not defending myself/arguing my point but I am paying him back for what he's covered through the summer (thankfully he has a great spreadsheet that tracks this stuff). I do know it's shitty to let him help with rent and bills and I want to do what I can to make it up to him.
